_doc: Per-lane freshness and plausibility checks. A breach logs a journal record with the sink's
MSGID_LANE_STALE, so it lands in the same incident queue as a systemd unit failure and the
This exists because the unit-failure queue only sees units that FAIL. Five of the analyst's
first sixteen findings were the other class: a lane that kept exiting 0 while going quietly
wrong — notifications silent for 57 h after a flat phone battery, local news 78% unenriched for
21 days, Ultrahuman coverage down to 4 h/day, Amex alerts arriving with no amount in them, the
statement archive ending in a false cliff. Green unit, degenerate data, nobody notified.
CAVEAT on the training lanes: a lane that is stale and an operator who did not train look
identical from here. Their windows are deliberately generous, and a breach means 'go and look',
Only lanes whose layout has actually been verified are listed. Declaring a path nobody checked
is the very failure this file is meant to catch — mail enrichment is absent for exactly that
reason. Local-news ARRIVAL was absent for that reason too until its store's layout was measured

lanes.name: notifications
lanes.note: The estate's only live Amex source. Went silent 57.1 h on 2026-07-29 (flat phone). RETIRED 2026-08-15: the amex-alert-detail lane (>=50% of Amex alerts must carry an amount) lived here and was removed. It did its job — it caught the 2026-08-06 changepoint after which Amex push alerts carry no amount or merchant — but that is now a PERMANENT state, so the check was asserting something nobody expects to be true again and fired hourly for six days. The open work is tracked as issue i-20260814-154101 (mo.lan/issues). Arrival of the notifications themselves is still guarded by this lane. Re-add a check here only to detect the amounts COMING BACK, which needs an inverted predicate this checker does not have today.

lanes.name: ultrahuman
lanes.note:
Ring data. `date` is written by the fetcher's own loop, so an empty 200 still yields a dated row — without `require` this lane reads ok on a table with no measurement in it. The four fields are payload-borne and independent: hr_points alone would be too strict (20 of 143 real days have none while still carrying steps/vo2_max). Coverage collapse is a separate problem, held by ultrahuman-coverage.

`active_minutes` was a fifth certifier and was REMOVED 2026-08-21: it is non-null on days whose payload carries no hr, no temp, no hrv and no steps series and an empty Sleep object, so it certified rows containing no measurement. Measured over the 154 rows of that date's artifact: it was the sole require-satisfying field on exactly 11 rows (2026-06-03..06-11, 2026-08-18..08-19), all with hr_points=0, and on none of the rows that carry samples — across the 95 payloads with samples and active_minutes>0 the steps series is never empty (min 87 points). So dropping it removes 11 false certifications and loses no true one, and it moves this lane's newest data-carrying row from 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-17, the last day with any samples. Whether the partner API echoes, extrapolates or measures active_minutes on those days was NOT established and does not matter here — the field stays in the artifact, it just no longer counts as proof the ring reported. Same class as the night_rhr echo closed in ea378fe.

lanes.name: technogym-cardio
lanes.note: Generous window: no training is indistinguishable from a stalled fetch.

lanes.name: localnews
lanes.note:
Does the Nextdoor crawl still store anything? The store is a service on webscout, not a file on this box, so no mtime here moves when the feed does. `scraped_ts` is written by the crawler when it stores a post, in UTC — confirmed against webscout's own journal, whose nextdoor-index.service run at 2026-09-10T10:35:33Z carries the 10:3x scrape slot.

The consumer's exit status is NOT a substitute and must never be read as one: localnews-distill.service pulls /api/pending, and a feed that has stored nothing leaves that queue empty, on which distill prints `annotated=0 timecode-only=0 failed=0` and exits 0. A green distill run is what a dead feed looks like.

18 h from the measured gap distribution over the store's whole 54-day history (187 scrapes, 2026-07-16..2026-09-08): the crawl runs 4x daily, median gap 5.02 h, and there is a hard shoulder at 9.1 h (the overnight 20:3x->05:3x slot) with exactly one gap between that and 58 h (a single 13.9 h). The three real silences are 58.0, 62.0 and 77.0 h. So 18 h clears every routine gap by 4+ h and every real stall by 40 h — it would have fired 3 times in 54 days, once per genuine stall, and it detects one ~40 h before the shortest of them ends.

STALE RIGHT NOW, and that is correct: nothing has been stored since 2026-09-08T15:34:34 while the crawler keeps running and exiting 0, logging `posts: 0 scraped, 0 new` at info on every run since. The crawl fault is on webscout (its CPU fell from ~19 s to ~2.3 s and memory from 1.1 G to ~330 M between the 15:34 and 20:30 runs of 2026-09-08 — a crawl that no longer renders or no longer authenticates); fixing that is not this lane's job. Being able to SEE it is.

lanes.name: ultrahuman-coverage
lanes.note:
Does a night carry enough HR samples to be worth reading? The ring is worn AT NIGHT ONLY -- deliberate, confirmed by the operator 2026-08-23 ("I rarely wear it during day except if I forget to take it off") -- so any 24 h-shaped test measures his habits, not the data.

That is what the previous predicate did. It required hr_span_h >= 12, and hr_span_h is FIRST-TO-LAST: a night-only wearer scores ~23.9 h when he puts the ring on before midnight (one point at 23:5x, one at 07:00, a 12.8 h hole between) and ~7 h when he puts it on after. So the lane was reporting what time he went to bed. It fired on 2026-08-21 at 5/9 against a 0.6 floor while every night in the window had a complete sleep summary and a normal ~110-point HR series -- an alarm about nothing, of the kind you learn to ignore. See moprox-memory/ultrahuman-span-is-not-coverage.

hr_points >= 40 tests DENSITY instead, which is what 'usable' means here, and it separates cleanly. Measured over the whole 156-row archive on 2026-08-23:
  Apr 0.87 | May 0.87 | Jun 0.43 | Jul 0.81 | Aug 1.00   (floor 0.6)
June is the real coverage collapse (median 19 hr_points, 16 nights with no sleep at all) and it fails by a wide margin; every healthy month clears the floor with room; the current 10-day window is 10/10. The old predicate scored Apr 0.80 / May 0.71 / Jun 0.27 / Jul 0.74 / Aug 0.91 -- it caught June too, but it was catching bedtime everywhere else.

40 rather than 60: 60 also works (Aug 0.96, Jun 0.37) but costs a night like 2026-08-17 (67 points, 8.6 min max gap -- a short but perfectly clean night) for nothing. `where` is unchanged and is inert: hr_span_h is non-null on all 19 zero-HR rows, so nothing is filtered out either way; it stays as documentation of intent. Row PRESENCE is the sibling `ultrahuman` lane's job, not this one's.

STILL NOT GUARDED, on purpose: hr_cov_5m and hr_gap_max_min, the interior view. Both are backfilled over the whole archive, and both are dominated by the deliberate daytime hole (median longest gap 12.8 h since July, ~2 h in April-May), so any floor over them measures wear habit again. If daytime wear ever becomes the norm, they are the right fields -- not this one.

lanes.name: amex-cycles
lanes.note:
The estate's third Amex source and the only one that LEADS the statement PDFs: per-billing-cycle net totals parsed out of the mail archive by finance/amex_cycles.py. It matters most right now because the live per-transaction lane is gone — Amex push alerts have carried no amount or merchant since 2026-08-06 (issue i-20260814-154101) and statements/amex stops at 2026-06-10 — so for recent cycles this artifact is the estate's ONLY Amex figure.

Why it needs a lane: nothing runs the producer. 8 textual mentions of amex_cycles across private-data and moprox-tooling, 0 invocations, and no installed timer names it; finance/build.py only READS the file, guarded by `except FileNotFoundError`, so a file that is present but stale is consumed in silence and reaches the gated /finance dashboard as if it were current. Measured twice: stale 25.42 days over 2026-08-18..2026-09-12, withholding cycle 2026-08 (GBP 4058.66, the year's high) — and stale AGAIN on 2026-10-03, stored newest cycle 2026-08 while replaying amex_cycles.py against the live mail tree yields 112 cycles ending 2026-09 at GBP 2857.58, cross-checked by both the reminder and the receipt. See moprox-memory/amex-cycles-artifact-has-no-producer.

`mail_date` and not `period`: it is the arrival clock — when the evidence for the newest cycle landed in the mailbox — which is what this lane is asking about. Amex mails the "Payment due reminder" on the 16th or 17th of every month, so over the 21 cycles from 2025-01 the gaps between consecutive mail_date values are 27..32 days: a current artifact's newest mail_date is never more than 32 days old. 1008 h = 42 days leaves 10 days of headroom over the widest routine gap. Today's real staleness (47 days) breaches; the regenerated artifact (16 days) reads ok.

CAVEAT, the same shape as the training lanes: from here, "nobody regenerated the artifact" and "Amex stopped mailing" look identical. The dormant-card years in this same file carry mail_date gaps of 60, 62, 62, 153 and 505 days, so if the card is ever genuinely retired this lane fires forever on a true fact. A breach means go and look; if the card is closed, RETIRE the lane rather than widen it — as the amex-alert-detail lane was retired on 2026-08-15.

This is a detector, not the fix. The producer still has no schedule, which needs a unit installed on a box this repo cannot reach; until then the lane turns a silent 25-day freeze into an incident within 42 days of the last mail. Layout verified 2026-10-03 by replaying the producer against the live mail tree under a redirected $HOME, per this file's rule that only verified layouts are listed. It is also the first lane for finance of any kind.

lanes.name: finance-statements
lanes.note:
The ONE file the gated /finance dashboard is built from: finance/build.py parses the Amex + Halifax statement PDFs into month×category×card aggregates and stamps `generated` into the result. Same root cause as the amex-cycles lane above — nothing runs the producer — but a separate artifact, and the one the operator actually reads.

Measured 2026-10-04: the committed statements.json was generated 2026-09-04T14:35:09Z, 714.0 h / 29.75 days ago. In that window three landed producer fixes never reached the dashboard: it carries `amex_cycles`=110 while finance/amex-cycles.json holds 111 and the mail archive yields 112, and it has neither `card_ceilings` nor `months_by_card`, both of which build.py at HEAD emits. So the dashboard is serving pre-fix output from a producer that was fixed a month ago, and nothing anywhere says so.

`json_stamp` and not `newest_file`: on this same file today the producer's own stamp says 714.0 h and the mtime says 568.3 h — the checkout rewrote the file 145.7 h after the producer last ran, so a mtime lane understates the staleness by six days and would read ok through most of a real freeze. That is the hazard check_json_newest's docstring names, and it is why neither git-tracked derived artifact in finance is watched on mtime. `json_newest` cannot do it either: these aggregates hold no list of dated records, only the one top-level scalar.

672 h = 28 days, from the artifact's own regeneration history. Over its nine commits the gaps between consecutive `generated` stamps are 0.01, 0.16, 0.01, 6.61, 0.01, 34.96, 1.25 and 24.19 days. 28 days fires on exactly one of them — 2026-07-06..2026-08-10, 34.96 d, the gap in which the dashboard was provably a whole statement behind — and clears the next widest (24.19 d, 580.4 h) by 91.6 h. Both cards statement monthly (Amex on an 11th→10th cycle, Halifax around the 3rd–5th), so a regeneration older than four weeks is certainly missing at least one.

CAVEAT, same shape as amex-cycles: this is a detector, not the fix. A breach means "run finance/build.py", not "something is broken", and it will keep firing until the producer has a schedule — which needs a unit installed on a box this repo cannot reach. Layout verified 2026-10-04: `generated` is present and is an integer epoch, which parse_ts accepts.

lanes.name: statements-amex
lanes.note:
Has the Amex statement archive grown? The two finance lanes above watch DERIVED artifacts (statements.json's `generated` stamp, amex-cycles.json's `mail_date`), so both go green the moment somebody runs the producer — over an input that stopped arriving. Nothing watched the input: of the 8 lanes in this file before 2026-10-05, 0 globbed a statement PDF, which is why the top two incidents in the queue going quiet on 2026-10-05 was the least informative possible outcome (moprox-memory/finance-statements-stale-dropped-a-month).

STALE RIGHT NOW, and that is the point: 18 PDFs, newest period 2026-05-11..2026-06-10, so the newest covered period ended 2819.6 h / 117 d ago as of 2026-10-05 and three Amex billing cycles from 2026-06-11 onward have no PDF. This matters more than it would on any other card: the live per-transaction lane is gone (push alerts have carried no amount since 2026-08-06, issue i-20260814-154101), so with the PDFs stopped too, recent Amex spend is known only as a monthly net from the mail cycle totals.

`filename_period` and not `newest_file`, measured on this exact glob 2026-10-05: mtime reports the newest file as 1431.1 h old and names `2026-01-11_2026-02-10.pdf`, a February statement, because the archive is git-tracked and a checkout rewrites every mtime without preserving their order. 1431.1 h is the age of the checkout — statements/halifax reports the same number — so a mtime lane here reads stale forever above any threshold and ok forever below it, whatever the archive does. The period in the filename is the only clock on this lane that the archive itself sets.

1344 h = 56 d, from the archive's own period structure rather than its commit history, which cannot be used: 16 of the 18 PDFs were bulk-imported on 2026-06-27/29, so the add-lag distribution is an import artifact. Amex closes on the 10th and the 17 consecutive period-end gaps are 28..31 d; the statement is available within about a week of the close (the payment reminder mail that amex_cycles.py parses arrives on the 16th-17th). So a healthy archive's newest period end peaks around 31 + 7 = 38 d just before the next PDF lands, and 56 d clears that by 18 d while firing on a single skipped cycle.

CAVEAT: this is a detector, not the fix. A breach means "go and download the statements", which needs a hand on a browser and a login this repo does not hold. If the card is ever genuinely closed, RETIRE the lane rather than widen it — as the amex-alert-detail lane was retired on 2026-08-15. Layout verified 2026-10-05 against the live archive.

lanes.name: statements-halifax
lanes.note:
The same question for the other card, and a separate lane because one archive growing while the other has stopped is exactly the state that must not average out: on 2026-10-05 Halifax was 2219.6 h / 92 d past its newest statement date (18 PDFs, newest 2026-07-05) while Amex was 117 d past its newest period end. Three Halifax statements from 2026-08 onward have no PDF.

Halifax names the file by the statement date alone (`2026-07-05.pdf`) where Amex names a range; the kind takes the newest YYYY-MM-DD in the basename, which is the end of the covered period under both conventions and needs no per-lane pattern.

1344 h = 56 d, the same as Amex and for the same reason. Halifax statements around the 3rd-5th, and over the 17 consecutive period-end gaps in the archive 16 are 28..33 d; the one outlier is 59 d, the missing 2025-03 statement, which is a real hole and the class of thing this lane is for. The single incremental add in the whole archive — 2026-07-05.pdf, committed 2026-07-06 — puts the availability lag at about a day here, so 33 + lag is comfortably inside 56 d.

CAVEAT as above: a breach means go and fetch them. Layout verified 2026-10-05 against the live archive.
